obligations.text: A manifest entry holds it (§ 2.3), and a response over the message binding (§ 1.2) MAY carry it.
A full fetch MUST return it, except for line items and packages the requester may not read (§ 5.8).
Consumers MUST compare byte for byte and MUST NOT normalize a value before comparing it.
Anyone MAY define an extension term.
An absent or unresolvable `registry_id` MUST NOT make a document malformed, and a consumer MUST ignore a resolved entry whose verified domain is not `domain`.
It MAY need authentication
For a `channel` (§ 5.1.1) or `cost_method` (§ 5.6.5) term, these effects are a MUST.
Manifest entries MUST match the current version of each proposal.
A seller that limits concurrent holds SHOULD declare the limit in `hold_limits`.
A seller MAY publish `https://<seller.domain>/.well-known/openproposal.json`, a `ProposalManifest`.
At least one of `ETag` and `Last-Modified` is REQUIRED, so buyers can poll cheaply.
A seller that declares `per_advertiser` MAY decline a hold request whose `requested_terms` names no advertiser.
REQUIRED when the request names a proposal the requester may read
A receiver SHOULD NOT parse it
A party that rejects a request MUST return `errors[]`, one or more `ErrorObject`s.
A seller's own entries MUST use its `seller.domain` as the key.
It MUST NOT keep a line item after removing fields from it.
It MUST keep `ext` unchanged when it stores or forwards the document.
A term the counterparty must understand to transact MUST NOT be an `ext` entry; it is a field or a vocabulary term.
Apart from an unknown term (§ 2.2), a receiver MAY skip a whole line item it cannot read, without assenting to it.
A receiver MUST ignore an `ext` entry it does not understand, and MUST NOT reject a document because of it.
An `ext` entry MUST NOT change the meaning of a field this specification defines.
A verifier MUST reject a `nonce` it has already seen from the same origin within the signature's lifetime, with `429`.
A requester that can't verify a response MAY refuse to write its own entry (§ 4.1.2).
On a `403` or `429`, a party SHOULD send `Accept-Signature` (RFC 9421 § 5.1) naming the components and parameters of § 2.8.2, and on a `503` it sends `Retry-After` instead.
The private keys in its `keys.json` are public test keys: section 6.8 says they "MUST NOT be used in production", and a verifier SHOULD reject them.
A party MAY require a signature on the routes it serves.
Signing is OPTIONAL in this specification: § 4.1.2 states what a signature shows, and `agreed` never depends on one.
A field on a line item MUST NOT inherit its value from the proposal or from a sibling line item.
A buyer MAY select and commit any subset of a proposal's `line_items[]`.

Because audiences, properties, formats, and `markets` are `selectable`, and a `settable` targeting `value` and buyer `exclusions` (§ 5.5) narrow delivery, `addressable_scale` and `availability` MUST be recomputed against the buyer's actual selection, values, and exclusions.
`availability` MUST also be recomputed against the `break_position` and `programs` options in effect.
`selectable`, `settable` and `supplied` fields MUST resolve without a round trip — everything needed to validate and price them is declared in the proposal.
The buyer MUST NOT alter the keys the seller declares beside them.

A producer MUST NOT write a Number that this serialization does not reproduce as the numeric value written; a Number with at most 15 significant digits inside the range of a double always does, and a document containing one that does not is invalid for this section.

A receiving party MUST recompute `record_digest` and compare it byte-for-byte before relying on a live `commitment` entry, over the line items as they stand plus the writes its `commit` carries (§ 5.6.1), or on a matching pair, from its agreed record (§ 4.1.2).
Strings, `Instant` values included, are hashed as that value; a party MUST NOT trim, normalize, or reformat a value it did not write.
Within the limits on a decline (§ 4.3.2, § 5.6.1), a party MAY refuse to write its own entry for any reason, including a counterparty message it cannot verify.
An entry that is not live stays in `assent[]`, and the line items it names MAY appear in a new `commitment` entry.
The seller MUST NOT interpret it (§ 5.6.1)
A seller MUST keep every version that a `negotiation_history[]` or `assent[]` entry names retrievable by `(proposal_id, version)` for as long as the proposal is retrievable.
A seller MAY edit a proposal in place only while its current version is not yet frozen (§ 4.1).
A seller MUST reject a `commit` that breaks either rule with `not_committable` (§ 2.4).
This check MUST be deterministic.
It asks for a change those options don't give, and the seller MAY decline it unless `terms_refs[]` (§ 5.8) gives it.
A seller MUST NOT name a domain it does not control.

A selling entity that controls several registrable domains SHOULD use the same `seller.domain` for every proposal it publishes as one seller; a seller that publishes proposals under several domains holds an Agent Registry entry for each, or the entry does not apply.
`proposal_template_id` MUST NOT be required for a buyer to transact.
A `counter` of `pricing[].list_rate` MAY also change `included[]`, with `paths[]` naming both
A `grant` or `counter` of a `request` on that entry MAY lower its `list_rate` or widen its `unit_bounds`.
A seller MAY revise a line item while an ask is open or a hold runs.
An ask it makes stale ends (rule 1), and the seller MUST release a `held` hold it makes stale or re-offer it at the new `version`, where `hold.status` stays `held`.
While it holds, a seller revision MUST NOT change that entry, `pricing_id` included, and MUST NOT end it sooner by moving `offer_window.end`.

The seller of an issued proposal MUST answer a resolved `commit` under it that arrives while the entry holds, on or after `offer_window.start`, and passes the checks of § 5.6.1 and any authority check the seller applies (§ 5.8): accept it, or decline it on an allowed ground.
The answer MUST come before the entry stops holding: otherwise silence works as a decline on no ground.
`status` unchanged; a later `commit` under that entry is rejected (§ 5.6.1), and the seller SHOULD `publish` or `withdraw`
The seller MUST serve a line item only on impressions of its `channel`.
Once the deal exists in `deal_origin`, the seller MUST record its ID as one `deal` entry on the line item.
The seller MUST NOT deliver the line item to an impression that does not match a key that is present.

A declared option is a delivery term: with an option in effect, the seller MUST serve the line item only into impressions that match one, and when the line item executes over OpenRTB 2.6, a bid request that offers its deal MUST carry `imp.video` or `imp.audio` values that match one.
A seller MUST NOT declare `slotinpod` 1, 2, or -1 unless it can guarantee that slot.
A consumer that checks MUST use this table, and confirms that sellers.json at `asi` lists `sid` as a `seller_id`, with `domain` equal to `seller.domain` where the entry carries `domain`.
A seller MUST NOT state a relationship its governing file, where one exists, does not support.
Each `seller_accounts[]` entry MUST be a record in the governing file.
Where that property's app store bars behavioral advertising (Apple's Kids Category, Google Play's Families policies), the line item MUST NOT carry `audiences`, and both flags MUST be false.
With `seller_allocated`, a buyer value MUST NOT name or exclude individual screens.
With an option in effect, the seller MUST serve the line item only into impressions that match one.

When the line item executes over OpenRTB 2.6, the seller MUST send the matched option's `content` values in `site.content` or `app.content`, under OpenRTB 2.6's key names, such as `livestream` for `live` and `contentrating` for `rating`.
`addressable_scale` and `availability` (§ 3.3) MUST be recomputed against conditions 1 and 3.
Synthetic events MAY be sent to test endpoints, or through a test mode that the receiving service documents as excluding those events from production measurement and delivery diagnostics.
An implementation MUST NOT report a check that was skipped or could not finish as passed.

The inspector MUST NOT request a destination or redirect that sends a production notification; it MAY use a separate inspection URL or the receiving service's documented test mode under the conditions below.
If the service cannot provide such a session, the creative MUST be inspected outside the stitched stream.
An implementation performing inspection MUST NOT send any production notification.
A preview served through server-side ad insertion MUST use a session in which the insertion service sends no production notifications.
An implementation MAY retrieve creative documents, follow VAST wrappers and inspect referenced media as needed for its checks.
A preview that executes creative or verification code MUST prevent that code from sending production notifications.
Inspection failures MUST be reported through diagnostics, without firing a production VAST `<Error>` or `verificationNotExecuted` URL.
When `spec_ref` is present, `spec` MUST equal the content of the version it names, and the format id SHOULD equal the `<collection>/<entry_id>` part of `spec_ref`.
A seller MUST reject an entry whose `store` it doesn't know, rather than apply it across stores, with `validation`
A seller MUST NOT present `best_effort` enforcement as a guarantee.
A seller MUST reject it deterministically rather than ignore it, with `not_offered`.
A seller MUST NOT disclose them to anyone but that buyer and the systems and vendors that enforce or verify them for this line item.
The seller MUST keep a rejection whose `retry` is not `same` at least until `offer_window.end`, or, on a proposal with no `offer_window.end`, for as long as it keeps the proposal.

The rejection MUST carry `expired` when `offer_window.end` or `price_valid_until` has passed, `stale_version` when the `commit` is stale, `not_committable` when a ground of that code applies (§ 2.4), and otherwise `record_mismatch`, so the buyer can fetch it again.
Reusing an `idempotency_key` with a different `Commit` MUST return `idempotency_conflict` and MUST NOT write an entry or change a `commitment`.
These checks MUST be deterministic: they depend only on the stored proposal, the `commit`, and the time the seller receives it.

For a replay from the same buyer of a `commit` the seller has already processed, with the same `idempotency_key` and an otherwise equal `Commit`, the seller MUST return the result as it now stands: the rejection, or the `CommitResult`.
A seller MAY decline a resolved `commitment` with a `decline` entry; the buyer MAY recompose.
It MUST NOT write a second `commitment` entry.
While a buyer's hold (§ 5.6.2) runs, the seller MUST NOT decline that buyer's `commitment` for lack of availability.
A value equal to the entry's means the line items have not changed and the buyer read the same terms, so the seller MAY accept, at the `version` the entry names.
A decline for lack of availability MUST state the `availability` of each line item it covers, recomputed against the buyer's composition; the seller's determination is authoritative.

The seller MUST reject a new `commit` whose `record_digest` differs from the recomputed value, that is stale (§ 4.1.3), whose proposal is past `offer_window.end`, or where the committed entry is past its `price_valid_until`.
It MAY remain on `expired` and `released`
A seller's answer MUST set `status` to `held` or `declined`.
A repeated request while `requested` or `held` MUST NOT start a second hold.
Every impression count that settles or invoices the line item MUST use its multipliers, and a committed `impressions` level (§ 5.7.1) settles on that source's count.
Impressions MUST be summed unrounded over each invoice period and rounded once.
A seller's own extension terms MUST use its `seller.domain` as the `<domain>`.
A receiver MUST treat an extension entry that breaks these rules as unavailable, not the line item as invalid.
A seller MUST decline a `commitment` whose term in effect conflicts with an accepted term on the same inventory and dates.
A seller MUST NOT preempt a line item that has no `preemption`, or for a reason that its `preemption` doesn't name.
The buyer MAY refuse a `makegood`, and the seller then offers the next.
A makegood MUST NOT run past `commitment.flight.end` without the buyer's consent.
A seller MAY offer that consent upfront in `remedy_terms`.
It means no remedy for any shortfall, and committed levels become targets, which an agent MUST NOT present as guaranteed.
It MUST treat that entry as unsatisfiable.
A consumer that does not know a `credential_type` MUST NOT treat the proposal or line item as invalid for that reason.
A seller MAY offer the same inventory through more than one.
A buyer MAY refuse a sole or last `makegood`, and § 5.7.1 then points at `remedy_terms`, whose keys describe only a makegood.

rules.statement: An entry named by both `include[]` and `exclude[]` is dropped, because exclusion wins. A narrowing that excludes every entry it includes takes nothing, which is a narrowing and not a contradiction.

`min` is at most `max`: numbers compare as numbers, timestamps as instants, and lengths of time as the lengths their written forms denote. A calendar month runs 28 to 31 days and a calendar year 365 or 366, so a pair of lengths that one form names in calendar units and the other in days is in order under every anchor, out of order under every anchor, or settled by the anchor the comparison names.
Each `included[]` entry, each `selected[]` entry and each `deltas` key names an option in `available[]`. A string option is named by its value, and an object option by its `id`.
No `deltas` key names an option in `included[]`. The base rate covers the included options, and `deltas` gives the change in price for each option beyond them.

`default` and `value` are each between `min` and `max`, inclusive, where that bound is present. A bound the seller leaves out bounds nothing, so a range with only a `min` bounds the value from below alone.
